text:
Abstract  
The user requested access to raw sequencing reads underlying GEO Series GSE309890 and whether those reads support assembly. To address this, we queried the NCBI GEO API via geo_series to retrieve series metadata and FTP links, and the NCBI SRA E-utilities via ncbi_sra_runs_for_project to list all raw read runs for the associated BioProject PRJNA1363958. We identified six Illumina HiSeq 4000 paired-end RNA-Seq runs, each averaging ~11–12 million spots at 300 bp read length, with download paths provided on the NCBI SRA FTP server. These reads are accessible for download and can be used for de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., with Trinity or SPAdes), but they derive from RNA-Seq (“Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing”) rather than whole-genome shotgun sequencing, limiting their utility for bacterial genome assembly. This result clarifies data availability for downstream analysis and highlights the need for appropriate DNA-based datasets for genome assembly.

I. Introduction  
Background. GSE309890 is a GEO Series profiling Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 under sertraline-induced stress (Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing). Raw sequence availability is crucial for custom analyses such as de novo assembly.  
Literature Review. No PubMed record is linked to GSE309890 [1].  
Knowledge Gap. It was unclear whether raw reads are accessible and suitable for assembly.  
Objective & Hypothesis. To determine availability of raw reads for GSE309890 and assess their suitability for downstream assembly; we hypothesized that raw RNA-Seq reads exist in SRA and could support transcriptome assembly but not full genome reconstruction.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. We used GEO’s esummary API to retrieve series metadata and FTP links, then fetched run-level information via SRA E-utilities for the corresponding BioProject.  
Materials.  
- GEO Series metadata: geo_series (GEO)  
- SRA run metadata: ncbi_sra_runs_for_project (SRA)  
Procedures.  
1. geo_series was called with accession=“GSE309890”, list_files=true to obtain series UID, FTP directory, and note on file types.  
2. ncbi_sra_runs_for_project was called with accession=“PRJNA1363958”, max_results=1000 to list all SRA runs.  
Statistical Analysis. We counted the number of runs (n=6), extracted per-run spot counts from the “spots” field, and noted the uniform average read length (avgLength=300 bp). Download URLs were taken directly from the “download_path” field.

III. Results  
Table 1 summarizes the six SRA runs.

Table 1: SRA runs associated with PRJNA1363958  
| Run        | Strategy | Layout | Spots      | AvgLength (bp) | Size (MB) | Download URL                                                                                                              |
|------------|----------|--------|------------|----------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SRR36018640 | RNA-Seq  | PAIRED | 11363329   | 300            | 894       | https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/.../SRR36018640.lite.1                                                        |
| SRR36018641 | RNA-Seq  | PAIRED | 11997182   | 300            | 948       | https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/.../SRR36018641.lite.1                                                        |
| SRR36018642 | RNA-Seq  | PAIRED | 11992461   | 300            | 955       | https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/.../SRR36018642.lite.1                                                        |
| SRR36018643 | RNA-Seq  | PAIRED | 11720219   | 300            | 926       | https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/.../SRR36018643.lite.1                                                        |
| SRR36018644 | RNA-Seq  | PAIRED | 10415434   | 300            | 801       | https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/.../SRR36018644.lite.1                                                        |
| SRR36018645 | RNA-Seq  | PAIRED | 11621726   | 300            | 917       | https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/.../SRR36018645.lite.1                                                        |

Findings. Six paired-end RNA-Seq runs are available, each ~11–12 million spots at 300 bp, accessible via SRA FTP. The GEO series supplementary files contain only processed expression matrices, not raw reads.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. Raw reads for GSE309890 are accessible through SRA under six run accessions, enabling de novo transcriptome assembly.  
Context. Series metadata [1] and SRA run list [2] confirm data type and access.  
Limitations. Data are RNA-Seq (transcriptomic), not genomic DNA sequencing, so they do not support full bacterial genome assembly; they are suitable for transcriptome reconstruction only.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. Researchers can download the six Illumina RNA-Seq datasets (paired-end, 300 bp) and perform transcriptome assembly. For genome assembly, corresponding whole-genome sequencing runs would be required; future queries might target DNA-Seq BioProjects for E. coli.  

References  
[1] GEO Series GSE309890 metadata; NCBI GEO: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0  
[2] SRA runinfo for BioProject PRJNA1363958; NCBI E-utilities efetch: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?rettype=runinfo&retmode=text&retmax=1000&WebEnv=MCID_6aac61b97a5a6c5e410ca57c&query_key=1&retstart=0&db=sra&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com  

Acknowledgments  
We thank NCBI GEO and NCBI SRA for providing the series metadata and raw sequencing run access.
